manual: Instructions for the Experiment: Comparison of Tablet, Capsule, and Liquid Medication Dissolving in WaterI. Basic Experiment Information1. Experiment Title: Tablet vs Capsule vs Liquid Medication Dissolving in Water2. Subject: Healthcare – Nursing (Pharmacology Basics)3. Experiment Objective: To visually compare the dissolution behaviors of tablet, capsule, and liquid medication forms in water, understand how dosage form affects onset and absorption, and strengthen nursing knowledge of medication administration.II. Experimental EquipmentThree identical clear glass cups, clean water (room temperature), one tablet medication (uncoated or film-coated), one capsule medication, one liquid medication (syrup or solution), dropper or measuring cup (for liquid), stable table surface, camera or phone with fixed focus for time-lapse recording.III. Experimental Procedure1. Preparation: Place three identical clear glasses side by side on a flat surface. Fill each glass with the same volume of clean water. Label positions visually as left, center, and right.2. Camera Setup: Fix the camera on a tripod facing the glasses. Lock focus and exposure to ensure consistent time-lapse recording.3. Core Operation:(1) Drop one tablet gently into the left glass.(2) Drop one capsule gently into the center glass.(3) Pour a measured amount of liquid medication into the right glass.4. Observation: Begin time-lapse recording immediately. Observe the changes in each glass without stirring.5. Conclusion: Stop recording once clear differences in dissolving or dispersing behavior are visible. Dispose of solutions properly and clean equipment.IV. Observation of Experimental Phenomena1. Initial State: All glasses contain clear, colorless water; medications are intact upon contact.2. Liquid Medication: Immediately disperses into the water, forming a uniformly colored solution.3. Tablet: Gradually absorbs water, sinks or rests at the bottom, then disintegrates into smaller particles before dissolving.4. Capsule: The outer shell softens and opens first, then releases internal powder or granules, which dissolve gradually.V. Summary of Experimental PrinciplesDifferent medication dosage forms are designed with different dissolution characteristics. Liquid medications require no disintegration and disperse fastest. Tablets must first disintegrate before dissolving. Capsules dissolve in two stages: shell dissolution followed by release and dissolution of contents. These differences influence drug onset time and are important considerations in nursing medication administration.
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target Concept: Comparison of medication dosage forms based on dissolution behavior in water, assuming basic pharmacological knowledge that form affects dissolution and absorption.Minimum Mechanistic Assumptions: Water acts as a solvent; no stirring is applied; room-temperature conditions; dosage forms behave according to standard pharmaceutical design.Phased Storyline: (1) Static setup with three identical water-filled glasses; (2) Sequential introduction of tablet, capsule, and liquid into left, center, and right glasses; (3) Accelerated time-lapse showing immediate dispersion of liquid, gradual tablet disintegration, and two-stage capsule dissolution; (4) End state highlighting clear comparative differences.Visibility and Perspective Constraints: Fixed camera angle, stable lighting, and unobstructed view of all three glasses are required to verify spatial order, temporal progression, and causal dissolution differences.
